Source. After signature-based importer selection, this call reads the exact 5914-byte witness into `buffer`; `TextFileToBuffer()` appends one trailing `0`, so the later parser copy sees 5915 bytes including the terminator.

`myParser.setBuffer(&buffer[0], buffer.size())` copies the importer buffer from step 1, including the appended terminator, into parser-owned `m_buffer`. All later `in` pointers and the crashing byte come from this copied buffer.

On the crashing recursive descent, this body-normalization step advances once from the current non-alphanumeric structural byte and leaves `in` on the next attacker byte that will be interpreted as a nested header start. The later UBSan index proves that byte's signed value is `-77` (raw byte `0xb3`), and `lookForNextToken()` does not skip it because it is not space, newline, or comma.

No primitive data token matches at the high-bit byte from step 3, so `type` remains `ddl_none` and the parser takes the complex-data branch. That recursive call reuses the same `in` value as the first character of another nested node header; there is no intervening check that nested headers begin with ASCII letters.

`parseNextNode()` enters `parseHeader()`, and `parseHeader()` immediately calls `parseIdentifier()` on the same byte from step 4. Before any other validation, `parseIdentifier()` asks whether the first identifier byte is numeric, so the attacker-controlled `0xb3` is passed as a signed `char` argument into `isNumeric()`.

Root cause and sink. On the witnessed call from step 5, `in` has signed value `-77` (raw byte `0xb3`). `static_cast<size_t>(in)` therefore becomes `18446744073709551539`, and the lookup indexes one of 256 `chartype_table` entries with that huge value. UBSan reports `runtime error: index 18446744073709551539 out of bounds for type 'const unsigned char [256]'` at this exact statement. The staged patch fixes the same path by checking `idx < sizeof(chartype_table)` before the table read.

anchors.note: First OpenGEX-side materialization of the attacker-controlled in-memory file into the importer buffer later copied into `OpenDDLParser`.
Root cause. `isNumeric()` widens a possibly signed `char` directly to `size_t` before indexing the 256-byte lookup table, with no cast to `unsigned char` or explicit bounds check.
UBSan crash site. The 256-entry character-class table is read with an out-of-range index derived from a signed high-bit `char`.
